functions.name: core_nvm_read
functions.signature: core_nvm_read(uint32_t offset, void * buf, uint32_t len)
functions.brief: Read bytes from NVM. Bytes never written read as CORE_NVM_ERASED (0xFF on Core.ST.L4 / W5, 0 on Core.ST.L0). Core.ST.H5 has no NVM yet: this always returns CORE_NVM_ERR_RANGE there.

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte offset within the NVM region (0 to CORE_NVM_SIZE-1).

functions.name: core_nvm_write
functions.signature: core_nvm_write(uint32_t offset, const void * data, uint32_t len)
functions.brief: Write bytes to NVM. On Core.ST.L4 / W5 (1 KB, flash-emulated) a write is atomic: after a reset or power loss the range reads all old or all new, and the data survives reflashing. Most writes take well under a millisecond; about one small write in a hundred (L4; one in 500 on the W5) compacts the store, which erases a flash page and stalls the Core.ST.L4 for ~22 ms. Core.ST.L0 writes its EEPROM byte by byte (~3.2 ms each). Core.ST.H5 has no NVM yet.

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte offset within the NVM region (0 to CORE_NVM_SIZE-1).

functions.name: core_nvm_erase_all
functions.brief: Erase the whole NVM region: every byte reads CORE_NVM_ERASED afterwards. Core.ST.L4 / W5: one page erase, or nothing if the region is already empty. Core.ST.L0: clears the EEPROM word by word (up to ~0.4 s; words already clear are skipped).

functions.name: core_nvm_size
functions.brief: Returns the total NVM size in bytes for this Core.

functions.name: core_nvm_read_byte
functions.brief: Read a single byte from NVM at `offset`. Returns the byte (0..255) on success or -1 on any error (offset out of range, NVM disabled). A byte never written reads 255 (0xFF) on Core.ST.L4 / W5 and 0 on Core.ST.L0. The signed return lets DSL programs branch on `< 0` without an out-pointer.

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte offset into the NVM region (Core.ST.L0: 0..511).

functions.name: core_nvm_write_byte
functions.brief: Write a single byte to NVM at `offset`. Returns 1 on success or -1 on any error (offset out of range, flash error, no NVM on this Core). Each call is one flash record on Core.ST.L4 / W5: fine for a setting or a boot counter, wasteful in a tight loop (see core_nvm.h on wear).

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte offset into the NVM region (Core.ST.L0: 0..511).

functions.name: ll_flash_erase_page
functions.brief: Erase a single flash page. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: ll_flash_program_dword
functions.signature: ll_flash_program_dword(uint32_t addr, uint32_t word0, uint32_t word1)
functions.brief: Program a double-word (8 bytes) at an 8-byte aligned address. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: ll_flash_program_qword
functions.brief: Program a quad-word (128-bit / 16 bytes) at a 16-byte aligned address. WBA55 and H5 program in 128-bit lines: the flash controller only completes (and clears BSY) once all four 32-bit words have been written, so all four must be issued before the busy wait — a partial write never completes. This is also the native granularity of the OTP region, so it serves both main flash and OTP (same PG bit + NSKEYR unlock; only the target address differs). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: ll_flash_wait_bsy
functions.brief: Spin until flash is not busy.
